samples.ref: Eh so a typical job- a day in my job is that- I look- I supervise court orders. So, if I’m allocated someone, then I have to undertake an interview with that person, eh, which is about, forty-five minutes long, and I have to assess their suitability to eh- to decide which, eh, work party that I would place them in. And eh, in terms of that risk assessment I’ve got to assess if they’ve got any substance misuse, eh, is the public going to be safe, eh, and you know, can- what- what eh kind of work does that person- what are they able to do really. Eh, and then once I assess them, I’ve got to upload all their- complete all the risk assessment paperwork, eh, upload it to their, eh, file, and eh then I need to check on the registers and make sure that my other clients have been attending their allocated placement days. Some have got placement days and some of them have just been told to, eh, attend and complete a minimum of eh unpaid work hours within a certain eh- per calendar month. And eh so, I’ve got to eh, you know, record their attendances, record their absences. If they haven’t been in, why haven’t they been in, I’ve got to contact them. Eh and of course, some of our clienteles will, eh, regularly have a different phone, so and eh, most of them won’t open their mail, so it can be quite challenging. Eh if they don’t eh you know get in touch with me, eh, depending on, eh, whether this is their first or their tenth absence, eh, I’ve got to eh, follow national guidelines and issue any disciplinary action. Eh and eh, have- organise, eh, appointments where we can have a review of the order, eh, try and see what supports they need, eh, to get through their order, and eh, all within- they’ve got to complete their hours all within, eh, the timescale as instructed by the court. Eh so, sometimes if people have medical, genuine reasons and they have submitted, eh, certificates to verify their absences, sometimes we need to eh, apply to the court and ask for an extension on their timescale, to allow them to fulfil their obligation to the court. And eh, sometimes if they don’t come in, don’t engage, eh, we ha- I have to return their order back to court, which- under breach- breach of order, and then that is classed as, eh, them committing another offence. So, eh I have to make sure that I’ve got enough evidence to do that, ‘cause sometimes we may be cited to appear in court to explain. Eh, so yeah, a lot of the same stuff, but different- different things happening every day. So, eh, that’s what I like about that it’s- it is a different- different cases, eh, so yeah.
